title: Ivo and the Regiment
premise: In 1914 England, Ivo Crane drives for suffragist Edith Marlowe and secretly reads the correspondence she smuggles for pacifist networks, memorizing addresses in case the war makes every letter a crime. When a shell-shocked soldier named Tomas Vane arrives bearing a letter in the handwriting of Captain Aurel Brandt—the man Ivo once promised to shelter if war ever came, and who is officially dead and posthumously branded a traitor—Ivo must decide whether invisibility is worth a broken oath. Hunting them is Major Corven, Edith's former ally turned intelligence officer, who suspects the Marlowe household is a conduit for enemy correspondence. Ivo smuggles Brandt, alive and disfigured, toward the coast while Edith sacrifices herself to buy time; the book ends with Ivo delivering the last letter, choosing exile over silence, and finding a fragile new belonging among the people the war discarded.
about_author: Paloma Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in provincial record offices. She writes historical fiction about the quiet people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Introduces Ivo's routine: driving Edith Marlowe, reading letters by lamplight, measuring everything by what can be carried in a coat. Establishes the household's rhythms and Ivo's careful invisibility. Emotional beat: the comfort—and loneliness—of a life built on not being noticed.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: three years earlier, Captain Aurel Brandt, a client's brother, shares a train compartment with Ivo and makes Ivo swear that if war comes, Ivo will carry a letter to a farmhouse in Kent. Emotional beat: the strange weight of being trusted by a stranger.

chapters.title: The Orders Come
chapters.summary: War is declared. Edith pivots the household from suffrage campaigning to pacifist relief work. Ivo reads the first censored letters and memorizes routes. Emotional beat: dread settling in like weather; the world begins measuring people in new units.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Tomas Vane, a discharged soldier, arrives at dusk asking for 'the driver who reads.' He carries a letter in Brandt's unmistakable hand. Ivo's POV, taut with fear. Emotional beat: the shock of being known after years of cultivated anonymity.

chapters.title: Dead Men Write Carefully
chapters.summary: The letter reveals Brandt survived a POW escape, is branded a traitor, and is hiding within a day's travel. Ivo must choose: burn the letter or honor the promise. Edith, unaware, notices Ivo's distraction. Emotional beat: guilt as a physical burden.

chapters.title: Major Corven Calls
chapters.summary: Corven, once Edith's ally in the suffrage fight, arrives ostensibly to warn her about mail interception; really to probe. Ivo serves tea and lies fluently for the first time. Emotional beat: the intoxicating and terrifying discovery that Ivo can lie well.

chapters.title: What the Letters Say
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, night scene. Ivo rereads years of saved letters and realizes the network Edith runs is larger than she admits—and that Ivo's memorized addresses could hang a dozen people. Emotional beat: complicity; knowledge as both shield and noose.

chapters.title: The Meeting at the Mill
chapters.summary: Ivo slips away to meet Vane at an abandoned mill and sees Brandt: half his face ruined, voice changed, but the handwriting the same. Brandt asks only for passage to the Kent farmhouse. Emotional beat: pity curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: A Household Divided
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. She suspects Ivo's absences and confronts him obliquely; Ivo deflects. Meanwhile Corven returns with a warrant to inspect correspondence. Emotional beat: the ache of lying to the one person who gave Ivo a place to belong.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Corven's men search the house and garage. Ivo hides Brandt's letter inside a punctured tire and endures the inspection at close range. Vane is detained for questioning. Emotional beat: terror in stillness; the price of a steady face.

chapters.title: Vane Breaks
chapters.summary: Ivo learns Vane, under pressure, has given Corven a partial description—not of Brandt, but of Ivo. The hunt now has a shape. Ivo decides they must move that week. Emotional beat: betrayal without malice; the machinery of survival grinding on innocents.

chapters.title: Confession at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Ivo finally tells Edith everything: the letters, the promise, Brandt. Instead of rage, she reveals she has suspected for chapters—and asks to help, splitting the risk. Emotional beat: relief and grief entangled; belonging redefined as shared danger.

chapters.title: The Plan
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. She will deliver herself and her papers to Corven as a diversion while Ivo drives Brandt to Kent under cover of a funeral cortege route. Emotional beat: cold clarity; love expressed as logistics.

chapters.title: The Funeral Road
chapters.summary: Ivo and Brandt travel in a borrowed hearse among mourners. Brandt talks about the promise, about why he trusted a stranger on a train. Checkpoints loom. Emotional beat: intimacy between the invisible and the erased.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Marleigh Bridge
chapters.summary: A roadblock; a young corporal recognizes the hearse's paperwork as false. Ivo talks his way through using Corven's own earlier words against him. Emotional beat: triumph with a bitter aftertaste—survival by becoming a better liar.

chapters.title: Edith Taken
chapters.summary: Ivo, from a distance, learns Edith has been arrested; Corven let the hearse through to follow it. The rescue plan was a trap in both directions. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out; guilt and gratitude at war.

chapters.title: The Farmhouse in Kent
chapters.summary: Ivo delivers Brandt to the farmhouse—promise kept—but finds the family gone and a neighbor ready to denounce any stranger. Brandt refuses to stay and insists on turning back for Edith. Emotional beat: the promise fulfilled feels hollow without the people left behind.

chapters.title: Corven's Offer
chapters.summary: Corven intercepts Ivo alone and offers a trade: Edith's release for the network's addresses Ivo has memorized. Ivo's POV, alone with the choice. Emotional beat: temptation as a mirror; power corrupting through mercy's shape.

chapters.title: The False Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo and Vane—freed and repentant—forge a partial ledger: real addresses of the already-dead and emigrated, enough to satisfy Corven's superiors. Emotional beat: defiance; fighting the machine with its own paperwork.

chapters.title: The Exchange at the Docks
chapters.summary: Climax. Night on the waterfront: the ledger for Edith, with Brandt appearing as bait to draw Corven's zeal into the open. Corven's superiors, embarrassed by his obsession, rein him in mid-exchange. Shots, chaos, Brandt wounded shielding Edith. Emotional beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Aftermath. Edith, released but ruined publicly, chooses exile; Brandt recovers under a dead man's name; Vane disappears into the ranks of the forgotten. Ivo packs one bag—the old measure—and burns the last unread letter unread. Emotional beat: grief with clean edges; letting go of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Last Address
chapters.summary: Ivo drives Edith and Brandt to the coast road at dawn, then keeps driving—not fleeing, but choosing the road where the discarded gather. Ivo writes the first letter ever addressed in Ivo's own hand. Emotional beat: belonging finally claimed, not granted; survival's price paid, and worth it.
